ChIPmentation: fast, robust, low-input ChIP-seq for histones and transcription factors.

chipmentation · Schmidl2015_original_ChIPmentation

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Lyse the fixed-cell pellet for 10 min on ice; spin lysed cells for 10 min at 1,000 × g, 4°C. Discard supernatant and resuspend nuclei pellet in Sonication Buffer.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
reagent
Cell Lysis Buffer: 50 mM HEPES/KOH pH 7.4, 140 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 10% glycerol, 0.5% NP-40, 0.25% Triton X-100, 1× protease inhibitors (Sigma).
reagent
Sonication Buffer: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.6, 1 mM EDTA, 0.1% SDS.
condition
10 min on ice for lysis; nuclei collection 1,000 × g, 10 min, 4°C.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Lyse fixed-cell pellet in the branch-specific buffer and sonicate in a 1 ml milliTUBE on a Covaris S220 for 30 min, duty cycle 5%, peak incident power 140 W, 200 cycles/burst, until most fragments are 200–700 bp. Centrifuge at full speed, 5 min, 4°C and transfer supernatant; the insoluble fraction is excluded.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
reagent
RIPA: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 140 mM NaCl, 1% Triton X-100, 0.1% SDS, 0.1% DOC, 1× protease inhibitors (Sigma).
equipment
Covaris S220; 1 ml milliTUBE (tube specification, not a separately stated lysis volume).
condition
30 min; duty 5%; peak incident power 140 W; 200 cycles/burst; most fragments 200–700 bp. Full-speed clarification for 5 min at 4°C.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Lyse fixed-cell pellet in the branch-specific buffer and sonicate in a 1 ml milliTUBE on a Covaris S220 for 20 min, duty cycle 5%, peak incident power 140 W, 200 cycles/burst, until most fragments are 200–700 bp. Supplement lysate with 1% Triton X-100 before clarification. Centrifuge at full speed, 5 min, 4°C and transfer supernatant; the insoluble fraction is excluded.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
reagent
L3B: 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA, 0.1% sodium deoxycholate, 0.5% N-lauroylsarcosine, 1× protease inhibitors (Sigma).
equipment
Covaris S220; 1 ml milliTUBE (tube specification, not a separately stated lysis volume).
condition
20 min; duty 5%; peak incident power 140 W; 200 cycles/burst; most fragments 200–700 bp. Full-speed clarification for 5 min at 4°C. Supplement lysate with 1% Triton X-100 before clarification.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Separately prepare antibody-conjugated beads: wash/resuspend twice in PBS/0.5% BSA/0.5% Tween-20, add one selected antibody, rotate >1 h at room temperature. Place beads on magnet, remove supernatant and add sonicated lysate. Incubate 3 h at 4°C on a rotator and retain enriched bead-bound chromatin.
Information effect
The chosen antibody assigns protein/histone-mark attribution to enriched DNA. This is a bulk library identity, not a cell barcode or UMI.
reagent
50 μl magnetic Protein A/G beads or 10 μl for low-input ChIPmentation; antibody-dependent resin. PBS with 0.5% BSA and 0.5% Tween-20.
reagent
Choose H3K4me1 1 μg/IP (Diagenode pAb-194-050), H3K36me3 1 μg/IP (Diagenode pAb-192-050), OR REST 10 μg/IP (Millipore 07-579).
condition
Antibody coupling >1 h at room temperature on rotator; chromatin capture 3 h at 4°C on rotator.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Separately wash beads twice in PBS/0.5% BSA; resuspend the antibody-appropriate Protein A/G beads in 200 μl PBS/0.5% BSA per IP. Couple one selected antibody by rotation >1 h at room temperature, then add blocked antibody-conjugated beads to chromatin and incubate 3 h at 4°C. Retain enriched bead-bound chromatin.
Information effect
The chosen antibody assigns protein/histone-mark attribution to enriched DNA. This is a bulk library identity, not a cell barcode or UMI.
reagent
50 μl magnetic Protein A/G beads or 10 μl for low-input ChIPmentation, in 200 μl PBS/0.5% BSA per IP; resin chosen according to antibody.
reagent
Choose H3K27ac 2 μg (Diagenode pAb-196-050), PU.1 5 μg/IP (Santa Cruz sc-352), CTCF 10 μl/IP (Millipore 07-729), OR GATA1 4 μg/IP, 2 μg for low-input (Abcam ab11852). CTCF mass is not inferred.
condition
Antibody binding >1 h at room temperature with rotation; chromatin capture 3 h at 4°C.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Process separate IgG reads using reported common skewer trimming, Bowtie2 hg19/GRCh37 --very-sensitive alignment with default multimapper allowance, and Picard duplicate marking/removal. Apply the ChIPmentation read-start offsets +4 bp on plus and −5 bp on minus to represent transposition centers. Retain the matched-background data identity.
Information effect
Creates the separate computational background input to target enrichment calling; does not move IgG material into target-IP material.
software
skewer; Bowtie2 --very-sensitive; Picard.
condition
Human hg19/GRCh37; multimapper handling at aligner default; nonduplicates used downstream; read starts +4 bp plus/−5 bp minus.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Sonicate resuspended nuclei in a 130 μl microTUBE (for up to 3 × 10^6 cells), Covaris S220, 12 min, duty cycle 2%, peak incident power 105 W, 200 cycles/burst, until most fragments are 200–700 bp. Centrifuge at full speed for 5 min at 4°C and transfer the chromatin supernatant. No size-measurement-driven adjustment rule is reported.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
equipment
Covaris S220 and 130 μl microTUBE; stated tube capacity is not a specified sample volume.
condition
12 min; duty cycle 2%; peak incident power 105 W; cycles per burst 200; most fragments 200–700 bp; clarification full speed, 5 min, 4°C.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Adjust clarified lysate to 200 μl/IP with the reported final buffer composition. Incubate with one chosen antibody overnight at 4°C on a rotator. In parallel, block 20 μl antibody-appropriate magnetic Protein A or Protein G beads overnight in PBS/0.1% BSA; add beads the next day for 2 h at 4°C on a rotator. Retain captured chromatin on beads.
Information effect
The chosen antibody assigns protein/histone-mark attribution to enriched DNA. This is a bulk library identity, not a cell barcode or UMI.
reagent
Choose H3K4me3 1 μg/IP (Diagenode pAb-003-050) OR H3K27me3 1 μg/IP (Diagenode pAb-195-050).
reagent
20 μl magnetic Protein A or Protein G beads (antibody-dependent); overnight blocking in PBS with 0.1% BSA.
reagent
Final 200 μl/IP: 20 mM HEPES, 0.1% SDS, 1% Triton X-100, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA.
condition
Antibody incubation overnight, 4°C; subsequent bead capture 2 h, 4°C; rotator.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Resuspend enriched beads in 30 μl tagmentation reaction buffer containing 1 μl Nextera Tagment DNA Enzyme. Incubate 10 min at 37°C in a thermocycler. Tn5 fragments and introduces sequencing-adapter tags while material remains in the immunoprecipitated bead-bound fraction; this precedes elution/crosslink reversal. No purified-ChIP-DNA tagmentation recipe is imported.
Information effect
Introduces sequencing-adapter tags into antibody-enriched genomic DNA. The source proposes chromatin protein protection as rationale for robustness; exact strand/end chemistry and a universal protection mechanism are not asserted.
reagent
30 μl buffer: 10 mM Tris pH 8.0, 5 mM MgCl2, containing 1 μl Tagment DNA Enzyme from Nextera DNA Sample Prep Kit (Illumina).
equipment
Thermocycler.
condition
37°C, 10 min.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Resuspend enriched beads in 30 μl tagmentation reaction buffer containing 1 μl Nextera Tagment DNA Enzyme. Incubate 10 min at 37°C in a thermocycler. Tn5 fragments and introduces sequencing-adapter tags while material remains in the immunoprecipitated bead-bound fraction; this precedes elution/crosslink reversal. No purified-ChIP-DNA tagmentation recipe is imported.
Information effect
Introduces sequencing-adapter tags into antibody-enriched genomic DNA. The source proposes chromatin protein protection as rationale for robustness; exact strand/end chemistry and a universal protection mechanism are not asserted.
reagent
30 μl buffer: 10 mM Tris pH 8.0, 5 mM MgCl2, containing 1 μl Tagment DNA Enzyme from Nextera DNA Sample Prep Kit (Illumina).
equipment
Thermocycler.
condition
37°C, 10 min.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Remove tagmentation reaction liquid and retain beads. Wash twice with 150 μl cold RIPA, using that branch’s formulation above, then resume the chosen ChIP protocol with its final washes: TE pH 8.0 twice; composition not specified. The author protocol recommends SDS/EDTA washing to inactivate/strip transposase; this explains the wash purpose without inventing a universal stop-buffer reaction.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
reagent
Post-tagmentation RIPA: two 150 μl cold washes, formulation as in o_wash_v2. TE pH 8.0 twice; composition not specified.
condition
SDS/EDTA-containing washes are recommended by author protocol for inactivation/removal of transposase when adapting ChIP recipes.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Remove tagmentation reaction liquid and retain beads. Wash twice with 150 μl cold TF-WBI, using that branch’s formulation above, then resume the chosen ChIP protocol with its final washes: TET twice: 0.2% Tween-20, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA. The author protocol recommends SDS/EDTA washing to inactivate/strip transposase; this explains the wash purpose without inventing a universal stop-buffer reaction.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
reagent
Post-tagmentation TF-WBI: two 150 μl cold washes, formulation as in o_wash_v3. TET twice: 0.2% Tween-20, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA.
condition
SDS/EDTA-containing washes are recommended by author protocol for inactivation/removal of transposase when adapting ChIP recipes.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Resuspend enriched beads in 30 μl tagmentation reaction buffer containing 1 μl Nextera Tagment DNA Enzyme. Incubate 10 min at 37°C in a thermocycler. Tn5 fragments and introduces sequencing-adapter tags while material remains in the immunoprecipitated bead-bound fraction; this precedes elution/crosslink reversal. No purified-ChIP-DNA tagmentation recipe is imported.
Information effect

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Remove tagmentation reaction liquid and retain beads. Wash twice with 150 μl cold WBI, using that branch’s formulation above, then resume the chosen ChIP protocol with its final washes: WBIV twice: 20 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA. The author protocol recommends SDS/EDTA washing to inactivate/strip transposase; this explains the wash purpose without inventing a universal stop-buffer reaction.
Information effect
Preserves specimen, selected target and ChIP recipe attribution through the retained fraction; discarded fractions do not become the library.
reagent
Post-tagmentation WBI: two 150 μl cold washes, formulation as in o_wash_v1. WBIV twice: 20 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, 0.5 mM EGTA.
condition
SDS/EDTA-containing washes are recommended by author protocol for inactivation/removal of transposase when adapting ChIP recipes.

Incubate retained beads in 70 μl elution buffer plus 2 μl NEB Proteinase K, 1 h at 55°C followed by 8 h at 65°C to reverse formaldehyde crosslinking. Transfer DNA-containing supernatant. Version 2 proceeds directly from this first transferred eluate to purification; the second extraction reported for versions 1/3 is not assigned here.
Information effect
Releases enriched tagged DNA from beads, digests protein and reverses crosslinks. DNA retains target attribution through its selection history.
reagent
Elution buffer: 0.5% SDS, 300 mM NaCl, 5 mM EDTA, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0. Proteinase K (NEB), 2 μl; stock activity unspecified.
condition
1 h at 55°C, 8 h at 65°C; direct purification of transferred eluate.

Action
For the ONE selected incoming ChIP recipe eluate (version 1 OR version 2 OR version 3, never a mixture of these alternatives), purify DNA using SPRI AMPure XP at sample:beads 1:2 OR Qiagen MinElute columns. The input list encodes mutually exclusive recipe choices, not simultaneous consumed fractions. These are alternative cleanups; do not combine both into a mandatory recipe.

Converges the selected alternative recipe at the same purified tagged-DNA interface while retaining branch/target identity. No physical pooling is performed.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Before preparing PCR, incubate KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix at 98°C for 45 s to activate the enzyme for successful nick translation in the first PCR step. Amplify the 1 μl library aliquot in a 10 μl qPCR with 0.15 μM primers, 1× SYBR Green and 5 μl 2× KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix. Program: 72°C 5 min, 98°C 30 s; 24 cycles of 98°C 10 s / 63°C 30 s / 72°C 30 s; final 72°C 1 min. Measure Cq to estimate enrichment cycles. Custom Nextera PCR primers as explicitly delegated to the ATAC-seq design inventory: common Ad1_noMX plus a selectable Ad2 design. All 24 Ad2 designs are available choices, not a combined reaction, a ChIPmentation sample-to-index map, loaded transposase strands, cell barcodes or UMIs. Inventory labels and literal sequences are retained separately in resources.
Information effect
Initial nick translation supports library amplification; SYBR fluorescence yields Cq. This analytical measurement governs production cycle count; analytical product does not establish a material input to sequencing.
reagent
10 μl analytical reaction: 1 μl library, 0.15 μM primers, 1× SYBR Green, 5 μl 2× KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix (Kapa Biosystems).

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Amplify retained purified library in a separate 50 μl reaction using 0.75 μM custom Nextera primers and 25 μl 2× KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix, with N cycles equal to the rounded-up analytical Cq. The reported KAPA preactivation is for successful nick translation in the first PCR step. The analytical 24-cycle program is not asserted as the production count or as a separately stated production thermal program. Custom Nextera PCR primers as explicitly delegated to the ATAC-seq design inventory: common Ad1_noMX plus a selectable Ad2 design. All 24 Ad2 designs are available choices, not a combined reaction, a ChIPmentation sample-to-index map, loaded transposase strands, cell barcodes or UMIs. Inventory labels and literal sequences are retained separately in resources.
Information effect
Amplifies adapter-tagged selected DNA and retains indexing introduced by the chosen primer design. This is the source’s cycle-count rule, not a claim of calibrated universal optimality.
reagent
50 μl final enrichment: 0.75 μM custom Nextera primers; 25 μl 2× KAPA HiFi HotStart ReadyMix. Designs specified in o_qpcr resources apply to this same primer inventory, without sample-index assignment.
condition
N = rounded-up Cq from analytical qPCR; ReadyMix activation 98°C for 45 s before PCR preparation for nick translation. Complete independent production program and DNA volume not specified.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Adjust ChIPmentation read starts: +4 bp for plus-strand alignments, −5 bp for minus-strand alignments, representing the center of the transposition event. The cited ATAC method supplies the rationale of dimeric Tn5 inserting two adapters 9 bp apart; this is attributed rationale, not full strand-level Nextera covalent chemistry.
Information effect
Changes data coordinates, not physical DNA. Antibody-selected genomic attribution persists. High-resolution structural interpretations are exploratory and require sequence-bias correction beyond the general enrichment endpoint.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Run MACS2 independently on biological replicates with bandwidth 200 bp and matched IgG as background. For broad histone marks H3K27me3/H3K36me3, additionally use --broad --nomodel --extsize 73 --pvalue 1e-3; keep the alternative TF/other-mark route without inventing broad flags.
Information effect
Infers genomic enrichment associated with the chosen antibody relative to separate IgG background; it does not establish absolute occupancy or universal TF footprints.
software
MACS2.
condition
Bandwidth 200 bp, matched IgG background; for H3K27me3/H3K36me3 additionally --broad --nomodel --extsize 73 --pvalue 1e-3. No automatic transfer of these broad flags to TFs/other marks.

Action, recipe and evidence
Action
Create genome-browser coverage with bedtools genomeCoverageBed; normalize each value to read count per base pair per million reads, then convert with UCSC bedGraphToBigWig. Default downstream nonduplicate restriction applies.
Information effect
Converts attributed alignments/coordinates into relative genomic signal. The normalization denominator is computational, not an absolute molecular standard.
software
bedtools genomeCoverageBed; UCSC Genome Browser bedGraphToBigWig.
condition
Read count per base pair per million reads.

Declared gaps and limitations

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:CHEM-G01

    The draft CHEM-G01 pending-inspection blocker is resolved at the material-route level by Supplementary Note p00039/p00040/p00043/p00044 (CHEM-F03–F15) and at the primer-inventory level by cited ATAC-seq supplement p00001/p00002 (CHEM-F16–F17); it is not evidence that these operations are unavailable. Residual noncritical preparation-recipe limits in the inspected Supplementary Note: glycine concentration/amount and quench time, several lysis/resuspension volumes, numerical full-speed centrifugation settings, version 2 TE composition, Proteinase K stock activity/concentration, and antibody-specific Protein A/G choice are not given there. These restrict reproduction as a complete SOP, not the supported cells→fixed chromatin→enriched beads→purified tagged DNA route. CTCF is stated as 10 μl/IP, so its mass remains unknown. No contradictory execution is asserted.

    Next evidence: Original version-specific preparation SOP/reagent sheets supplying these missing quantities and antibody-resin assignments; for a chosen new specimen/target, validated ChIP optimization conditions. Preserve the source-supported boundaries meanwhile.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:CHEM-G02

    Exact molecular-end detail remains limited: main p00004/p00016/p00018 and supplement p00005 establish Tn5 fragmentation/adapter tagging and initial nick translation; the inspected ATAC-seq dependency and PCR oligo inventory do not specify the original kit’s enzyme activity/concentration, loaded transposon strand sequences, transferred strand ends or full covalent intermediate. PCR-primer sequences must not be relabelled as loaded Tn5 adapters. The named-kit tagmentation and amplification boundary is supported for frozen scope; a claim about exact end chemistry or a custom transposase substitution is not established.

    Next evidence: Contemporaneous Illumina Nextera DNA Sample Prep Kit loaded-adapter/enzyme technical documentation and a source linking its exact strand architecture to this original ChIPmentation variant; do not replace with later kit or remembered defaults.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:CHEM-G03

    Library-primer and amplification assignment limit: main p00018 links custom Nextera primers to the cited ATAC-seq source, whose table provides 25 oligo designs, but no general ChIPmentation sample-to-Ad2 map or index-read orientation is specified. Main p00018 explicitly gives the analytical qPCR thermal program and a separate production composition/Cq cycle rule; it does not independently state a complete final-PCR thermal program or volume of purified DNA transferred into that reaction. The ATAC dependency p00017 has a different preamplification/qPCR architecture and cannot silently fill these details. This does not block the general indexed-library amplification route or require historical sample reconstruction.

    Next evidence: Original ChIPmentation amplification/indexing SOP clarifying the production program, DNA input volume and primer-pair/index-read convention for a selected library design. Historical sample maps are needed only for claims about a particular executed sample.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:CHEM-G04

    SPRI internal detail limit: main p00018 reports 0.7:1 removal of >600 bp DNA followed by 2:1 recovery of remaining DNA, supporting first-supernatant/second-bead retention. It does not clarify whether the second ratio is an incremental addition or final total in the continued reaction, nor provide final bead washes/elution volume or a lower size bound. Supplementary Note purification alternatives likewise name AMPure/MinElute without full manufacturer internals. These are noncritical detail limits for the published separation boundary; no invented bead-volume arithmetic is claimed.

    Next evidence: Original two-step SPRI size-selection SOP defining the second ratio’s volume reference and final recovery, plus contemporaneous AMPure XP/MinElute instructions for explicitly delegated internal cleanup details.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:CHEM-G05

    Matched-control preparation boundary: main p00020 requires matched IgG background and Table 2 p00004 shows independent ChIPmentation IgG libraries, but the inspected target-antibody recipes do not specify IgG identity/mass or which of versions 1–3 generated each matched control. A separate sequenced control boundary and its data role are established; an exact control reaction or universal matching rule is not. This is nonblocking for the declared general protocol architecture but limits any claim about fully specified or historically executed control preparation.

    Next evidence: Original IgG-control SOP stating antibody species/isotype/catalogue/amount, ChIP preparation branch, specimen/input matching and control-library processing; exact pairing is required only if claiming a specific executed comparison.

  • Non-blocking · chemistry:CHEM-G06

    Sequencing/interpretation internal settings: inspected main p00018/p00020/p00021 and Table 2 identify platform, read-format examples, alignment/peak-calling rules and enrichment readouts, but do not supply a general pooling/loading recipe, demultiplexing/index-mismatch settings, all software versions/default realizations, a numerical replicate-consistency decision threshold, or QC-triggered rerun rule. Qubit measurements in main p00017/p00019 concern other protocols; they cannot support a ChIPmentation loading controller. These details do not block the source-described sequencing→target-enrichment boundary; no exact numerical reproduction or adaptive loading behavior is claimed.

    Next evidence: Original facility library submission/loading and demultiplexing SOP, applicable software versions/commands and stated replicate/QC decision criteria if a reproducible numerical analysis or adaptive control claim is required. For general architecture, retain the reported boundaries and qualified rules.

  • Non-blocking · information:G01

    Primer identity is resolved in I06. Remaining decoding detail is not specified in inspected ChIPmentation amplification/sequencing Methods or the delegated inventory: index choice for a library, pooling/index-read orientation and length, demultiplexing software and mismatch rules. The supported boundary is indexed library → sequence reads, not an executable demultiplexing protocol or cell/UMI decoder. This does not block the frozen general workflow; exact decoding execution remains unsupported.

    Next evidence: Original ChIPmentation indexing/sequencing instructions specifying index-read format, sample/index assignment rule and demultiplexing settings. A historical sample map is not required for the generic boundary.

  • Non-blocking · information:G02

    I05 records the rounded-up-Cq rule, but the inspected amplification Methods do not state Cq fluorescence threshold/baseline conventions or an absolute standard curve, nor explicitly repeat a thermocycler program for the separate production reaction. The 24-cycle program is assigned to analytical qPCR, not asserted as the production program. These are noncritical detail limits for the source-described boundary, but prevent a fully executable amplification SOP or numerical calibration claim.

    Next evidence: Original-version amplification worksheet detailing Cq conventions and the production thermocycler program; calibration standards only if absolute quantitation is claimed.

  • Non-blocking · information:G03

    I11 resolves matched-IgG background and separate IgG libraries; inspected target-antibody recipes do not identify IgG amount/species, exact preparation or matching criteria. I13 resolves a separate Nextera genomic-DNA bias reference, but its preparation and positional scaling before exponentiation are not specified in the bioinformatics paragraph. Keep these as control-data boundaries with unknown internals, not mixed spike-ins. This does not block qualified general enrichment or the documented optional correction rule; exact control execution/numerical reproduction is unsupported.

    Next evidence: Original matched-IgG and Nextera genomic-DNA control preparation instructions, plus the positional-background normalization specification if reproducing footprint correction.

  • Non-blocking · information:G04

    Sources establish Tn5 adapter introduction, the dependency rationale of adapters inserted 9 bp apart, PCR nick translation and the custom amplification oligos. Inspected passages do not fully specify original commercial transposome-loaded oligos, strand-level covalent end structures or every fill-in intermediate. No detailed junction chemistry beyond reported changes is asserted. This is a noncritical internal-detail limit for the frozen architecture; the tagmentation-to-purified-library interface is supported.

    Next evidence: Original Nextera DNA Sample Prep chemistry documentation or an explicitly applicable molecular schematic identifying loaded adapter strands and post-insertion/repair products.

  • Non-blocking · information:G05

    Replicate consistency precedes merging in I11, but the inspected processing paragraph supplies overlap metrics without a numerical acceptance cutoff or an action for failure. Preserve the reported gate without inventing a rerun decision, minimum FRiP, or adaptive sequencing-depth rule. This does not block the source-described peak-calling workflow.

    Next evidence: An original replicate-quality decision protocol specifying acceptance criteria and resulting actions if an operational controller is required.

  • Non-blocking · information:G06

    I17 records a final pre-sequencing QC boundary mentioned in supplementary cost accounting. The inspected ChIPmentation amplification/sequencing paragraph and that cost note do not identify final concentration/size measurement methods, standards, pass thresholds or how measurements determine pooling/loading. Qubit and the >1,200 bp cut are assigned to the separate ATAC procedure in I16. This missing inspection recipe is noncritical for the general library-to-sequencing boundary; a specific quantitation or adaptive loading claim would be unsupported.

    Next evidence: Original-version ChIPmentation final-library QC and sequencing-submission instructions specifying measured quantities, instrument/assay, any calibrants and any actual pooling/loading decision rule.

  • Non-blocking · integrator_wash_counts

    Version 2 RIPA-LiCl wash has no explicit count in inspected Supplementary Note p00040; do not infer two washes from neighboring buffers. Several branch-specific wash volumes are not separately repeated. The specified sequence through LiCl and return to final TE is supported, so this is a recipe-detail gap rather than a missing material route.

    Next evidence: Original version 2 wash worksheet specifying RIPA-LiCl count and per-buffer volumes.

s_cells · material

Cells entering one selected target-specific ChIP recipe. Cultured K562 cells and isolated PBMCs are reported study contexts, not universal input requirements. Demonstrated low-input profiles used 10,000 cells for H3K4me3/H3K27me3 and 100,000 for GATA1/CTCF; these are examples rather than universal minimums. Antibody quality limits feasibility and new antibodies/cell types may require ChIP optimization.

d_transposition_coordinates · data

Target-library nonduplicate alignments with read-start coordinates represented as transposition centers (+4 bp plus, −5 bp minus). Retains genomic position/strand and target attribution. Insertion patterns alone do not guarantee TF footprints or direct nucleosome positioning; sequence bias and assay-specific reference anchors matter. The published nucleosome comparison used NucleoATAC dyads inferred from separate GM12878 ATAC-seq, rather than independently calling dyads from ChIPmentation.

Modules: optional navigation groups
Specimen quantity and selection of a ChIP alternative · Module m_specimen

Starts at cellular specimens; one target/recipe is selected for a given library. Target-specific low-input demonstrations limit applicability, not universal cell minimums.

  • o_count · Count cells
  • o_fix_v1 · Fix and collect cells: version 1
  • o_fix_v2 · Fix and collect cells: version 2
  • o_fix_v3 · Fix and collect cells: version 3
Prepare and enrich target-associated chromatin · Module m_capture

Ends at LiCl-washed enriched chromatin on beads. Distinct lysis, sonication, antibody and wash recipes remain alternatives; no hybrid histone/TF recipe is formed.

  • o_nuclei_v1 · Lyse cells and isolate nuclei: version 1
  • o_shear_v1 · Sonicate and clarify chromatin: version 1
  • o_shear_v2 · Lyse, sonicate and clarify chromatin: version 2
  • o_shear_v3 · Lyse, sonicate and clarify chromatin: version 3
  • o_capture_v1 · Capture target chromatin: version 1
  • o_capture_v2 · Capture target chromatin: version 2
  • o_capture_v3 · Capture target chromatin: version 3
  • o_wash_v1 · Wash enriched beads through LiCl: version 1
  • o_wash_v2 · Wash enriched beads through LiCl: version 2
  • o_wash_v3 · Wash enriched beads through LiCl: version 3
Introduce sequencing-adapter tags before DNA release · Module m_tagment

Begins at enriched bead-bound chromatin and ends at washed tagmented chromatin, preserving branch-specific wash identities around the common tagmentation chemistry.

  • o_pre_tag_v1 · Exchange bead wash buffer: version 1
  • o_tag_v1 · Tagment enriched chromatin on beads: version 1
  • o_post_tag_v1 · Remove reaction and finish bead washes: version 1
  • o_pre_tag_v2 · Exchange bead wash buffer: version 2
  • o_tag_v2 · Tagment enriched chromatin on beads: version 2
  • o_post_tag_v2 · Remove reaction and finish bead washes: version 2
  • o_pre_tag_v3 · Exchange bead wash buffer: version 3
  • o_tag_v3 · Tagment enriched chromatin on beads: version 3
  • o_post_tag_v3 · Remove reaction and finish bead washes: version 3
Release and purify target-attributed tagged DNA · Module m_release

Deproteinization/crosslink reversal changes the material from chromatin on beads to purified tagged DNA. Versions 1/3 re-extract; version 2 does not inherit that step. Alternative outputs converge without physical pooling.

  • o_release_v1 · Elute and reverse crosslinks: version 1
  • o_release_v2 · Elute and reverse crosslinks: version 2
  • o_release_v3 · Elute and reverse crosslinks: version 3
  • o_purify_selected · Purify the selected recipe eluate
Analytical aliquot and controlled production enrichment · Module m_library

Separates measurement material from production material; measured Cq controls production cycle count. Final size-selected library and incompletely specified QC bound sequencing entry.

  • o_aliquot · Take analytical library aliquot
  • o_qpcr · Perform analytical nick translation and qPCR
  • o_pcr · Enrich production library using measured Cq
  • o_remove_long · Remove long PCR fragments
  • o_recover_library · Recover remaining DNA after size exclusion
  • o_final_qc · Inspect final library at reported QC boundary
Sequence target and independent IgG libraries · Module m_reads

Turns attributed physical libraries into processed target and background data. IgG preparation is a reported boundary with unknown internals, not an invented target-recipe assignment.

  • o_sequence · Sequence enriched library
  • o_igg_boundary · Prepare separate IgG control at supported boundary
  • o_igg_sequence · Sequence separate IgG control library
  • o_trim · Trim sequence reads
  • o_align · Align reads to human reference
  • o_deduplicate · Mark and remove duplicate reads
  • o_igg_process · Process IgG background reads
  • o_shift · Represent Tn5 transposition centers
Interpret relative genomic enrichment · Module m_enrichment

Produces normalized genomic tracks, independently/background-called peaks, consistency-gated merged peaks and FRiP. Exploratory structural applications do not become required enrichment protocol steps.

  • o_tracks · Generate normalized genomic signal tracks
  • o_peaks_replicate · Call enrichment peaks per replicate
  • o_check_replicates · Assess replicate consistency
  • o_merge_replicates · Merge consistent biological-replicate data
  • o_peaks_merged · Call merged-replicate enrichment peaks
  • o_frip · Measure enrichment signal-to-noise
